title: Machine-learning prioritization and CRISPR knockout identify OsWOX13 as a rice heat-tolerance regulator
summary: Meta-transcriptomic comparison of heat-tolerant and susceptible rice genotypes yielded 409 meta-differentially expressed genes. Random-forest and XGBoost feature ranking with SHAP independently prioritized OsWOX13; CRISPR/Cas9 knockout lines showed lower survival under heat stress (~20% versus ~60% in wild type) and delayed flowering, with accompanying changes in ABA, oxidative-stress markers and stress/flowering-associated proteins.
ai_technology: Random forest and XGBoost models with SHAP feature attribution
organization: Hainan University; Guizhou University; National Institute of Agricultural Science, Rural Development Administration (Republic of Korea); Pusan National University; Kookmin University

evidence.tested: Meta-transcriptomic comparison of heat-tolerant and susceptible rice genotypes yielded 409 meta-differentially expressed genes.
evidence.unknown: The PubMed primary abstract supports gene prioritization and knockout evidence, but does not establish detailed direct molecular targets or field-level yield effects. Reported survival figures concern the study's heat-stress condition and experimental lines; this is not evidence of breeding performance or resilience in field environments. Mechanistic pathway interpretations remain limited to associated physiological/proteomic measurements.
evidence.ai_role: The models prioritized stress-associated genes from meta-transcriptomic differences; OsWOX13 was among the top-ranked genes in both models. The team tested its predicted positive role using CRISPR/Cas9 knockout, followed by heat-stress survival, flowering, physiology and proteomic assays.
